title: Washington’s Elise Woodward believed to be first female radio play-by-play announcer in the FBS
content:
A new voice will serve as the soundtrack for Washington football this fall, and she’s set to make some history along the way.

The University of Washington announced Tuesday that Elise Woodward will be the program’s new radio play-by-play announcer starting with the 2026 season, making her what is believed to be the first woman in the FBS to hold such a role.

Woodward, who is also the play-by-play voice for the Portland Fire in the WNBA, has been a sideline reporter for the Huskies for more than 20 years. She roamed the sidelines during Washington’s run to the national championship game at the end of the 2023 season, and she’ll jump right into the action with her new gig this fall when the Huskies play rival Washington State in the Apple Cup in Week 1.

“Having the opportunity to be the voice of University of Washington football is the honor of my lifetime,” Woodward said in a statement released by the school. “As a Dawg, I take so much pride in the rich history and tradition of Husky football. I am so thankful for the last 23 seasons that I spent on the sidelines, but I’m also beyond excited to trade in my rain gear for the warmth of the Bob Rondeau radio booth.”

Woodward, an Oregon native, played basketball for the Huskies from 1993 to 1997 and captained the team as a senior. She has a versatile background in broadcasting, having worked primarily in basketball and football but also in volleyball, women’s gymnastics, men’s soccer, track and field, MLB and the NFL. She graduated from Washington with a degree in broadcast journalism. Woodward replaces Tony Castricone, who left the job after nine years to become the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ radio play-by-play announcer.

Women have become an integral part of football broadcasts over the years, but few handle play-by-play duties. Woodward will join some strong company, though, in ESPN’s Beth Mowins and Courtney Lyle, who have both done college football play-by-play for the network, and Lisa Byington, who made history in 2017 as the first woman to take on play-by-play duties for a football game on the Big Ten Network.

With quarterback Demond Williams Jr. returning to Washington for 2026, Woodward should have plenty to chronicle with a team that won nine games a season ago and enters Year 3 under head coach Jedd Fisch.

“Elise has built an outstanding career as a sports broadcaster at both the national and local levels,” Washington athletic director Pat Chun said in a statement. “She has established herself as a trusted voice within the Husky community through her years covering UW Football, Women’s Basketball, and Seattle sports. She knows this university, its traditions, and the rich history of this role. We couldn’t be more excited to have Elise carry forward the legacy of being the voice of Husky Football.”
